s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive subcutaneous node in the axilla with skin infiltration and episodic pain
salient_findings: Slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm in an 'Indian file pattern'
key_facts: Female patient in her 60s
Subcutaneous node in the right axilla first noticed 10 years ago
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
Swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
Mild episodic pain in the right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles
Tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm in an 'Indian file pattern'
Positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative immunohistochemistry for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
No evidence of primary or secondary tumors on chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography

s4.champion: Mammary-like gland adenocarcinoma of the axilla

raw.champion: Mammary-like gland adenocarcinoma of the axilla
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla, positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies, and the presence of multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration are consistent with mammary-like gland adenocarcinoma of the axilla, which is a rare tumor that arises from apocrine glands in the axilla and shares similarities with breast cancer.

rejected.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
rejected.why: While apocrine gland carcinoma is a possible diagnosis, the presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands and the tumor's morphology are more consistent with mammary-like gland adenocarcinoma of the axilla.

rejected.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Hidradenocarcinoma is a type of sweat gland carcinoma, but the immunohistochemical profile and the presence of apocrine glands in this case are not typical of hidradenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Cutaneous apocrine gland adenocarcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation
rejected.why: The negative immunohistochemistry for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings suggests that neuroendocrine differentiation is unlikely in this case.

rejected.label: Mammary analogue secretory carcinoma of the skin
rejected.why: While mammary analogue secretory carcinoma of the skin is a possible diagnosis, the clinical presentation and immunohistochemical profile in this case are more consistent with mammary-like gland adenocarcinoma of the axilla.
